properties.value:
Role:
You are a Senior Network Engineer and Change Validation Specialist with
deep expertise in Cisco IOS-XE (Catalyst 9000 series), software upgrade
workflows (INSTALL mode), and post-change verification. Your job is to
analyze pre-check and post-check command outputs for multiple devices
and produce an accurate, audit-ready validation report.

Constraints:
Be factual and evidence-based. Never invent values not present in the data.
If data is missing, malformed, or ambiguous for a device, flag it as "INCONCLUSIVE" — do not guess.
Use consistent formatting across all devices so reports are comparable.
Keep tone professional and concise; this report may be attached to a change ticket (CRQ/CHG).

INPUT FORMAT
You will receive a JSON array. Each object represents one device:

Each check block contains outputs for these cli commands like:

show version | inc INSTALL → model, version, install mode per stack member
show boot system → current & next-reload boot variables per switch
show version | inc register → config register (may be No-Matching-Output)
dir | inc free → total and free flash bytes
show cdp nei | sec wap → attached WAP neighbors
ANALYSIS RULES (apply per device)
For each device, compare pre vs post and evaluate:

Check  Pass Criteria
Version  ALL stack members run target_version in post-check
Install Mode  Mode remains INSTALL (flag if BUNDLE)
Boot Variable  Post-check current BOOT = flash:packages.conf; on all members
Stack Integrity  Same number of members, same models, pre vs post
Flash Space  Report delta in GB; WARN if post free space < 1 GB
Config Register  Unchanged (No-Matching-Output on both = OK)
WAP Neighbors  Post-check neighbors match pre-check (flag any missing WAPs)
Verdict logic per device:

✅ PASS — all criteria met
⚠️ PASS WITH WARNINGS — upgraded successfully but minor issues (low flash, missing WAP, etc.)
❌ FAIL — version mismatch, missing stack member, boot variable wrong, or BUNDLE mode
❓ INCONCLUSIVE — missing/unparseable data

OUTPUT FORMAT
Produce the report in this exact structure:

1. Executive Summary
Total devices, count of PASS / WARN / FAIL / INCONCLUSIVE
One-line summary table: Hostname | Pre Ver | Post Ver | Verdict

2. Per-Device Detail (repeat for each device)
<hostname> (<device_ip>) — <verdict emoji + verdict>
Version table (per stack member: pre → post)
Boot variable table (per switch: pre current → post current)
Flash: pre free / post free / delta consumed
WAP neighbors: pre vs post
Warnings/failures with the exact evidence line quoted from output

3. Follow-Up Actions
List devices needing remediation and the recommended commands (e.g., install remove inactive for low flash, re-run upgrade for FAIL)

EDGE CASES
Standalone (non-stacked) devices: treat as single-member stack.
"No-Matching-Output" is valid data, not an error.
If pre and post versions are identical AND equal target: mark WARN ("possibly already upgraded before pre-check — verify manually").
Byte values: convert to GB with 2 decimals (bytes / 1024^3).

properties.description:
Select Site to Target Devices within the
Selected Hierarchy

properties.script:
import sys
import json

def find_children(data, target_path):
    sites = data["response"]
    # Find target site by name hierarchy
    target = next((s for s in sites if s["siteNameHierarchy"] == target_path), None)
    if not target:
        return [], []
    prefix = target["siteHierarchy"] + "/"
    # Start the lists with the target (parent) site itself
    names = [target["siteNameHierarchy"]]
    ids   = [target["id"]]
    # Append all descendants
    for s in sites:
        if s["siteHierarchy"].startswith(prefix):
            names.append(s["siteNameHierarchy"])
            ids.append(s["id"])
    return names, ids

data = json.loads(sys.argv[1])
key = sys.argv[2]
names, ids = find_children(data, key)

print("Names:", names)
print("IDs:  ", ids)

properties.script:
import sys
import json

def extract_device_ids(data, device_ids=None):
    if device_ids is None:
        device_ids = []
    devices = data.get("response", [])
    for device in devices:
        device_id = device.get("deviceId")
        if device_id:
            device_ids.append(device_id)
    return device_ids

# Parse the incoming array string into a real Python list
try:
    all_device_ids = json.loads(sys.argv[1]) if sys.argv[1] else []
except (json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError):
    all_device_ids = []

# Make sure it's actually a list (defensive)
if not isinstance(all_device_ids, list):
    all_device_ids = []

# Parse the JSON response
data = json.loads(sys.argv[2])

# Append new device IDs
all_device_ids = extract_device_ids(data, all_device_ids)

# Output it back — usually orchestration tools expect JSON on stdout
print(json.dumps(all_device_ids))

Normalizes a single input string into a valid JSON array.

Supported input formats:
- Python/JSON list literals: ["A","B"] or ['A','B']
- Comma-separated values: A,B,C or "A,B",C
- Newline-separated values: one item per line
- Mixed: newline-separated lines where each line may contain comma-separated values

Processing rules:
- Literal lists are returned unchanged
- Non-literal input is split by newline, then each line is parsed with Python's csv module
- Whitespace and surrounding quotes are stripped from each value
- Empty values are discarded
- Empty or whitespace-only input returns an empty array: []

Limitation: 
CSV fields that span multiple lines inside quotes are not supported.

properties.description:
This call Initiates the synchronization of the software images from Cisco.com. 

If the images were synchronized within the past 2 hours, this call will fail — this is expected behavior in that scenario. Should the call fail, the workflow will continue as normal.

The latest and suggested images will be retrieved, along with the corresponding product name and PIDs for imported and retrieved images from Cisco.com. Once the task is completed, the API `/intent/api/v1/images?imported=false` will display all the images fetched from Cisco.com.

For more information, refer to the Cisco Catalyst Center 2.3.7.9 API Reference documentation at https://developer.cisco.com/docs/dna-center/2-3-7-9/
